data.title: Eastern International receives Nasdaq non-compliance notice
data.description:
Eastern International (ELOG) announced on Friday that the company received a Nasdaq letter, notifying it that the company no longer meets the minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on Nasdaq. 

The company highlighted that the notification has no immediate effect on the listing of its ordinary shares. 

In accordance with Nasdaq Marketplace Rules, the company has a period of 180 calendar days from the date of notification until March 9, 2027, to regain compliance with the Minimum Bid Price Requirement. 

The company said it intends to continue actively monitoring the bid price for its ordinary shares between now and the expiration of the compliance period and will consider all available options to resolve the deficiency and regain compliance with the Minimum Bid Price Requirement.

Source: press release

data.title: Olin Winchester wins $788.4M U.S. Army ammunition contract
data.description:
• Olin Winchester, a business division of Olin (OLN) announced on Friday that it won a $788.4M firm-fixed-price IDIQ contract for the procurement of 5.56mm, 7.62mm and .50-caliber ammunition.
  • The work locations and funding are to be determined as individual orders are issued.
  • The contract is expected to be completed on September 10, 2031.
  • Army Contracting Command is the contracting activity.

data.title: Boeing wins $13.4B U.S. Air Force contract ceiling boost for FMS work
data.description:
• Boeing (BA) won a $13.4B contract ceiling modification for the FMS work.
  • The modification raises the total contract ceiling to $19.1B from $5.7B.
  • The contract covers FMS to Japan and Israel, with additional countries potentially included in the future.
  • Moreover, the work will be performed in Seattle, Washington, and is expected to run through April 28, 2035.
  • No funds were obligated at the time of the award, meaning the higher ceiling does not represent an immediate $13.4B cash booking.
  • The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center is the contracting activity.

data.title: JPMorgan cut off lending to Situational Awareness after AI debacle - FT
data.description:
JPMorgan (JPM) ended its lending activity for Leopold Aschenbrenner’s hedge fund Situational Awareness after the investor suffered severe losses in July.

JPMorgan was one of the prime lenders to Situational Awareness through its prime brokerage. After the losses were disclosed, the bank informed the hedge fund that it would terminate their lending relationship, according to a  Financial Times report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

JPMorgan and Situational Awareness declined to comment to the FT.

Situational Awareness has recently started working with specialist brokerage Clear Street, according to the report. Clear Street declined to comment to the FT.

The news comes after CNBC reported earlier Friday that Situational Awareness, the artificial-intelligence-focused hedge fund founded by former OpenAI researcher Aschenbrenner, is again active in the markets through call option buying.

Situational Awareness has been buying options positions in stocks including Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Bloom Energy (BE), Coreweave (CRWV), SK Hynix (SKHY), and Sandisk (SNDK), CNBC's David Faber reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. The moves were made last week and early this week.

Aschenbrenner's latest moves come after Situational Awareness sold a large portion of its public-equity portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel after suffering steep losses during a recent technology sell-off in late July.

data.title: JPMorgan, BofA, others vying to manage Anthropic employees' wealth after IPO - report
data.description:
Wall Street banks are said to be racing to manage the wealth that Anthropic's employees are expected to earn after its initial public offering.

Goldman Sachs (GS), Bank of America (BAC), Bank of New York Mellon (BNY), JPMorgan Chase (JPM), and Wells Fargo (WFC) are in talks with the AI company over sending its employees a list of financial advisers, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.

Anthropic had called for details about fees, services, and other aspects of wealth management, according to some of the sources who asked not to be identified because the communications are private.

The company's IPO is expected to create vast wealth for its employees, Bloomberg reported on Friday.

data.title: Rainier Acquisition announces separation of IPO units
data.description:
• Rainier Acquisition (RNAQU) will allow holders to separately trade Class A ordinary shares and warrants from its IPO units beginning September 14, 2026.
  • The separated securities will begin trading on Nasdaq on September 15 under RNAQ (shares) and RNAQW (warrants), while unseparated units will continue trading as RNAQU.
  • Each unit contains one Class A ordinary share and one-quarter of a redeemable warrant, with only whole warrants eligible for trading and exercise.
  • Each whole warrant gives holders the right to purchase one Class A ordinary share at $11.50.
  • The IPO, including the underwriter’s full over-allotment option, consisted of 8.625M units and raised $86.25M in gross proceeds.
  • The full $86.25M, or $10 per unit, was placed in the company’s trust account.

data.title: Restaurant Brands renews $1B buyback plan for up to 34.4M shares
data.description:
• Restaurant Brands (QSR) said on Friday that the Toronto Stock Exchange approved the renewal of its normal course issuer bid (NCIB) for common shares.
  • Under the renewed NCIB, it can repurchase up to 34.4M shares, representing 10% of its public float, from September 16, 2026, through September 15, 2027.
  • The buyback is part of the company's $1B share repurchase authorization, which runs through September 30, 2027.
  • Under its previous buyback plan, the company repurchased 2.91M shares at an average price of about $74.97 per share through September 10, 2026.
  • The company said future buybacks will depend on market conditions, share price, and other factors.
  • Moreover, the repurchased shares will be cancelled and funded from the company's cash resources.
  • The company has also established an automatic purchase plan that allows its broker to continue buying shares during management-imposed blackout periods.

data.title: ON Semiconductor rebounds after recent weakness, jumps 8%
data.description:
Shares of ON Semiconductor (ON), a provider of intelligent power and sensing solutions for automotive, industrial, and AI data-center applications, advanced just over 8% on Friday. This marked a rebound after a stretch of weakness that left the stock down more than 12% over the prior month.

Shares finished the day at $76.14, a gain of $5.97 on the session.

data.title: UAE modifies 5-GW Stargate data center project in wake of Iran war: report
data.description:
The United Arab Emirates is modifying the plan for its massive 5GW data center due in part to the ongoing war between the U.S. and Iran, according to Reuters.

The $30B data center project, which is one of the largest in the world, was originally planned for a 10-square-mile campus in Abu Dhabi. However, due to potential threats from Iran and others in the region, the project will now likely feature a network of smaller data centers scattered throughout the country, the report said, citing sources with knowledge of the situation.

Partners in the the UAE Stargate campus include Oracle (ORCL), OpenAI (OPENAI), Cisco (CSCO) and Nvidia (NVDA). The project is being led by G42. It is part of a goal to diversify the country's economy and transform it into a regional AI hub. As part of the project, the UAE cut its ties with China.

In March, Iran conducted attacks on Amazon Web Services (AMZN) data centers in Dubai and Bahrain.

The UAE still plans to build out the first phase of its Stargate project at the Abu Dhabi campus, but it will likely be equipped to defend itself from aerial attacks, the report said. The remaining phases will be scattered across the desert nation, with those housing sensitive data possibly built underground or in mountains.

data.title: Chip stocks lead Nasdaq's weekly gains; Amgen plunges after trial setback
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) climbed on Friday alongside major Wall Street indexes after the latest consumer inflation report came in largely in line with expectations. It closed +0.96% higher after jumping by over 1% earlier in the day.

However, the tech-heavy index dipped 0.65% for the holiday-shortened week with markets closed on Monday, on account of Labor Day.

For the entire week, semiconductor stocks led the gains, with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) up more than 13%. Marvell Technology (MRVL) and Intel (INTC) were the second and third-highest gainers. Earlier in the week, Piper Sandler initiated coverage on chip stocks, assigning Overweight ratings to the above stocks, among others.

Amgen (AMGN) led the detractors after Novartis (NVS) announced a late-stage trial setback for a heart disease therapy the Swiss company is developing with Ionis Pharmaceuticals (IONS). Thomson Reuters (TRI) dragged nearly 13% for the week after announcing a cybersecurity incident involving its C-Track court management platform.

Top five gainers of the week:

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) +13.15%

Marvell Technology (MRVL) +13.06%

Intel (INTC) +12.29%

Teradyne (TER) +12.15%

Lumentum Holdings (LITE) +9.40%

Top five decliners of the week:

Amgen (AMGN) -15.03%

Thomson Reuters (TRI) -12.89%

Adobe (ADBE) -11.73%

Shopify (SHOP) -11.72%
